messages:
maria: quick follow-up from the RFC review — I sketched an alternative approach to the dequant fusion opset that might avoid some ABI churn and simplify runtime dispatch. TL;DR: introduce an atomic 'dequant_op' with a small opset describing src layout, scale metadata, and target data-type, and let kernel authors opt into fusing it with attention kernels.

kevin: short question — how does this differ from the earlier proposal where the runtime did dequant then called fast_attention?

maria: the main diff is we don't mandate a dequant pass as a separate IR op. Instead the kernel signature can include an optional encoded dequant descriptor. If absent, runtime does the dequant. If present, the kernel performs dequant in-stream and directly writes into attn-compatible buffers. That lets us keep a single codepath for fused vs unfused kernels.

ashley: sounds promising. Does the descriptor include per-head scales? we need per-head, per-group, and possibly per-tensor quant params for exported FP8/INT4 checkpoints.

maria: yes — descriptor fields: src_dtype (fp8/int8/int4), layout (packedQKV | qkv_interleaved | separate), scale_type (per_tensor|per_head|per_block), scale_ptr (optional), zero_point_ptr (optional), scale_multiplier (float fallback). plus flags: in_place_ok, requires_alignment.

kevin: hmm, what about alignment/stride guarantees? fused kernels benefit a lot from 64B alignment and 128-bit loads. If runtime can't guarantee that for customer buffers, we lose perf.

maria: right. descriptor will include an alignment hint and runtime will either pin buffer or copy to an aligned scratch. There's a flag 'requires_aligned_scratch' so kernel can tell runtime to pre-copy.

simon: how do we express mixed precision i/o? some attention kernels read qkv in INT4, compute in FP16, write FP16 KV cache. Are we adding conversions beyond dequant (like upcast + permute)?

maria: descriptor supports a small 'post_ops' bitfield. entries like UPCAST_FP16, TRANSPOSE_HEADS, PACK_KV_CACHE. Kernel implementers can consume those hints. The idea is to keep the descriptor small but expressive.

ashley: testing concern — we need deterministic small-unit tests for fused path vs runtime-dequant+kernel to catch numerical diffs. will add to eval harness but we should define an acceptance threshold for FP8->FP16 differences.

kevin: perf question: is there an expected perf delta from fused dequant vs runtime copy+dequant? I recall fused win ~1.6x on A100 for long contexts, but for short seq lengths cost of extra complexity sometimes regresses.

runtime-bot: perf run 1774501250: fused-dequant-attn-vs-seq: seq=256, bsz=4, model=redwood-3B-quant, fuse=on -> 1.48x median, 1.33x p95; seq=64 -> 1.12x median, 0.98x p95.

maria: thanks bot — that matches expectation. We should encode a policy: only prefer fused kernels when seq >= 128 or when kernel reports lower overhead via a microbenchmark API.

kevin: about the kernel ABI — propose kernel func signature like: int fused_attn(void* ctx, const dequant_desc* dq, const attn_desc* a, void* outputs). Keep dq nullable. ctx is runtime handle for buffers/allocs. Return codes: 0 OK, >0 fallback codes.

ashley: i'd avoid raw pointers in public ABI; use 64-bit IDs (buffer handles) so private deployments can validate and we can do IPC. kernels in the hosted runtime can still map handles to pointers.

maria: good call. change to: fused_attn(runtime_handle_t ctx, dequant_desc_id dq_id, attn_desc_id a_id, buffer_id out_id). With dq_id == 0 meaning no fusion. Runtime exposes a small registry for transient descriptors.

kevin: descriptor registry lifecycle sounds tricky. who frees them?

maria: ephemeral descriptors are pinned to the request lifetime. runtime creates descriptor, registers id, kernel can read via ctx API. after request completes runtime deletes entry. Persistent descriptors used for offline-compiled kernels can be registered at load time.

simon: fallback behavior: if a fused kernel returns FALLBACK_UNALIGNED or FALLBACK_NO_MEM we should auto-try the non-fused path. Need to ensure we don't pay double-cost by copying then running again in some pathological cases.

maria: runtime policy: if kernel returns FALLBACK_UNALIGNED and the descriptor had requires_aligned_scratch==true, runtime will allocate aligned scratch and retry once. only then fall back to non-fused if retry fails. avoids double-copy loops.

ashley: also need clear tracing so perf plotting ties request -> kernel choice -> copy size. Console should show per-request whether fused or fallback took place.

kevin: on unit tests: add randomized fuzz that generates descriptors (layouts/scales) and compares fused kernel output to reference path. If we do per-head scaling we must test edge cases: tiny heads, scale=0, denorms.

maria: agreed. add 'golden' harness target that runs K=1024 random examples and reports max absolute diff and relative quantized stats. We'll block merges if max_abs_diff > 1e-2 for FP16 outputs unless model-level override.

simon: shipping concern — what's the rollout story for Dedicated/Private customers who may have old kernels compiled without dequant descriptor support? We need graceful compatibility layer.

maria: runtime will keep the legacy path. For model tags that indicate quantized artifacts, runtime will prefer kernels that support the dequant descriptor. If none are available, do runtime dequant+legacy kernel. We'll publish a compatibility matrix.

kevin: one more: batching & continuous batching. If multiple requests have different descriptors, how to batch? we can only batch similar descriptors. runtime should group by descriptor key (dtype+layout+post_ops) and batch accordingly.

maria: yes — propose descriptor hashing function (small 64-bit key) that we use as a routing/batching key. Add fields that are allowed to differ (scale_ptr contents) and still batch under conditions — e.g., per-tensor vs per-head scales can't batch together. We'll document the groupable combinations.

ashley: proto idea: add a 'group_tolerance' field for approximate batching where per-head scales differ but are similar within epsilon; might be useful for OLTP but complicated. maybe MVP skip.

maria: skip for now, file as follow-up. action items: 1) @kevin please draft minimal kernel ABI header with handles + return codes. 2) @ashley add test harness plan + acceptance thresholds. 3) @simon write compatibility matrix stub for Dedicated/Private. 4) i'll update perf policy and descriptor schema and post RFC patch.

kevin: taking 1). will post PR by EOD.

ashley: taking 2).

simon: taking 3).

maria: thanks all. If anyone wants me to pair on the descriptor schema ping me. :rocket:
